Write an MDB object in parquet files

Source: R/generics.R, R/parquetMDB-conversions.R
as_parquetMDB.Rd

Write an MDB object in parquet files

Usage

as_parquetMDB(
  x,
  path,
  htmlModel = TRUE,
  compression = "zstd",
  maxCol = PQ_MAX_COL,
  by = 10^7,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'memoMDB'
as_parquetMDB(
  x,
  path,
  htmlModel = TRUE,
  compression = "zstd",
  maxCol = PQ_MAX_COL,
  by = 10^7,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fileMDB'
as_parquetMDB(
  x,
  path,
  htmlModel = TRUE,
  compression = "zstd",
  maxCol = PQ_MAX_COL,
  by = 10^7,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'chMDB'
as_parquetMDB(
  x,
  path,
  htmlModel = TRUE,
  compression = "zstd",
  maxCol = PQ_MAX_COL,
  by = 10^7,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'metaMDB'
as_parquetMDB(
  x,
  path,
  htmlModel = TRUE,
  compression = "zstd",
  maxCol = PQ_MAX_COL,
  by = 10^7,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'parquetMDB'
as_parquetMDB(
  x,
  path,
  htmlModel = TRUE,
  compression = "zstd",
  maxCol = PQ_MAX_COL,
  by = 10^7,
  rewrite = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

an MDB object

path

the path where the MDB should be written

htmlModel

a logical. If TRUE (default) the model is also plotted in an html file.

compression

the compression algorithm used in parquet files (default: "zstd"). See arrow::write_parquet() for available values.

maxCol

the maximum number of columns for writing a dense matrix in a wide format: one column in the parquet file per column of the matrix (default: 1000). Dense matrices with more columns are written in a long format (see parquetMDB). Sparse matrices are always written in a long format.

by

the size of the batch: number of records to write together (default: 10^7)

...

method specific parameters

rewrite

a single logical only used when x is a parquetMDB. If FALSE (default) the parquet files are copied as they are: compression and maxCol are not taken into account. If TRUE, the files are written again according to compression and maxCol.

Value

A parquetMDB object.

Details

For fileMDB, the text files are converted in parquet files by the arrow package without loading the data in R. When a file cannot be converted this way (e.g. values not supported by the arrow reader), it is read by batches in R as a fallback and a message is displayed. Dense matrices with more than maxCol columns are also converted by batches in R.

See also

read_parquetMDB(), as_fileMDB()
